name: H5N1 bird flu
value: Sporadic US cases; Oregon case 19 Nov
summary: Oregon confirms a mild dairy-linked human H5 case on 19 Nov; US cases remain animal-linked with no human-to-human spread
state: Oregon confirmed its first human avian influenza case of 2026 on 19 Nov, linked to cattle at a Morrow County dairy farm; the person had mild symptoms and the state says risk to the public is extremely low (Oregon Health Authority). ECDC counted 74 US human H5 cases since April 2024 as of 5 Nov (ECDC). Searches to 26 Nov found no human cluster or person-to-person spread, so cases remain sporadic and Normal holds.
for_you: Risk to the public is low; people who work with poultry or dairy cattle should follow CDC or UKHSA guidance on protective equipment.

sources.title: Oregon Health Authority — OHA confirms state's first human case of avian influenza of 2026

why: H5N1 is the flu strain scientists most fear could become a pandemic; it has spread to mammals and dairy cattle.
drivers: Human cases, mammal-to-mammal spread, mutations, surveillance.

rubric.watch: Human clusters under investigation, rising human cases, or new mammalian species spread.
